input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
input.rationale: Compliant at the fallback; no redline proposed. (1) Customer convenience right is present in substance: Section 17(b) (p0118) lets Sparkling terminate "at any time" on ninety (90) calendar days' written notice, subject only to ceasing use and certifying return/destruction of the Software. It does not use the label "for convenience" or "without cause", but no cause, default, breach or other trigger is required, so the right is unconditional — substance controls over phrasing, and any deterministic keyword check on "for convenience"/"without cause" is a wording artefact here. (2) Notice period of 90 days sits at the top of the playbook fallback range (60-90 days). (3) No early-termination fee, penalty, forfeiture or accelerated-payment obligation attaches to Section 17(b), which is better than the fallback's tolerance of a fee up to three months' fees. (4) No Vendor convenience right exists anywhere: Section 17 permits termination only by Sparkling under 17(b) or by either party for insolvency events / material default uncured after thirty days (17(c), p0128), and the Section 10 maintenance term (renewable one-year) contains no Garman right to walk away, suspend or decline service at will — so the walk-away trigger (Vendor convenience termination on under 90 days' notice) is absent. (5) Section 17(a) (p0117) keeps the Agreement and licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year committed lock-in from which Sparkling needs an exit. Sub-elements short of the preferred position, noted as observations only and not escalated: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and 17(b) does not expressly require a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (the fee-return remedy at p0128 applies only on termination for Garman's default). Fee exposure is limited by the annual maintenance term, so these are minor gaps against preferred rather than failures of the fallback.
